documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
24F transferring care after a move to Sunderland. Works as an administrative assistant.

HbSS sickle cell disease since birth. Usual hemoglobin runs mid-9s per her. Takes folic acid 1 mg daily. No hospital stays reported. Not on hydroxyurea.

HIV: tested positive at her old clinic in April of this year. Was given a name of an HIV clinic there but never went, then moved. Has never taken antiretrovirals. Feels well, no fevers, weight steady, no thrush, no rashes.

Allergy: sulfamethoxazole, listed by her old clinic as an anaphylaxis risk. She does not remember the episode herself.

Family: younger brother has sickle cell disease. Mom and dad both carry the trait. A paternal aunt has lupus.
Social: never smoked, no alcohol, no drug use. Single.

Exam: well appearing. Sclerae anicteric. Oropharynx clear, no thrush. No lymphadenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rash. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected.

A/P
1. HIV, untreated. Explained that treatment keeps her well and protects partners. Referral to Infectious Disease placed today. She agrees to call them.
2. HbSS. CBC and CMP today. Continue folic acid.
3. Health maintenance: Pap today. PCV20 given (sickle cell and HIV both qualify). Flu and COVID when available this fall. PHQ-2 negative.
Return in about 4 months.

documents.title: Immunization Record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: PCV20 0.5 mL IM, left deltoid. VIS reviewed. Tolerated well, no reaction during 15 minute wait.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jada, your blood counts are right where you said they usually run, hemoglobin 9.5. Kidney function and liver enzymes are normal. Bilirubin is a little high at 1.9, which is expected with sickle cell. Nothing to change. The Pap result takes about a week. Please do call the infectious disease clinic if you haven't yet.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap came back normal. With HIV we repeat it every year, so we'll do the next one next summer.

documents.title: RE: Pap result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thank you!! ID clinic said first opening is october, i'm on the list

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after work for influenza and the 2025-26 COVID vaccine. Afebrile, no illness today. Influenza right deltoid, COVID left deltoid. Sulfa allergy noted, not relevant to either. Waited 15 min without issue.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Home test positive last night. LMP 1/13/2026, so about 5 weeks. Planned enough, she says, and she is happy about it. Mild nausea in the mornings, no bleeding, no cramping, no pain crises since we met. Still on folic acid 1 mg. Never made it to the ID clinic visit in the fall.

O: Vitals as charted. Well, comfortable. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Urine hCG positive in office.

A/P
Intrauterine pregnancy presumed, ~5 wk, EDD 10/20/2026. High risk: HbSS and untreated HIV.
- Referred to high-risk obstetrics today; asked them for an early slot.
- Prenatal vitamin daily, keep folic acid 1 mg.
- HIV: talked plainly about why treatment matters now, for her and for the baby. ID referral from August is still open; she will call them this week, and OB will know too.
- Hydration, avoid getting chilled, call early for any pain or fever.

documents.title: Prenatal Visit Letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside high-risk obstetrics clinic. Prenatal visit 04/23/2026. Received 04/28/2026.

Dear colleague,

We saw Ms. Owusu, 25, G1, for her scheduled prenatal visit at 14 weeks 2 days by her January 13 LMP (EDD 10/20/2026). She is followed here for HbSS sickle cell disease and HIV in pregnancy.

Her main question today was how likely she is to pass HIV to the baby. Her HIV was found about a year ago and she has not started treatment. Apart from the sickle cell disease and HIV, her history is unremarkable. Never smoker, no alcohol. Works as an administrative assistant.

Medications: folic acid 1 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis risk).
Family history: brother with sickle cell disease; both parents carry sickle cell trait; paternal aunt with lupus.

Vital signs normal. Examination unremarkable.

Labs 04/23: HIV-1 RNA 15,000 copies/mL. CD4 450 cells/mm3. CBC stable at her baseline, hemoglobin 9.5. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative, hepatitis C antibody nonreactive.

Assessment: HIV infection complicating pregnancy, second trimester, untreated; HbSS sickle cell disease.

We told her that with effective treatment and an undetectable viral load the chance of transmission to the baby is very low, and that the sooner treatment starts the better. We are coordinating with Infectious Disease for antiretroviral therapy. Continue folic acid and prenatal vitamin. Return in 4 weeks.

High-risk obstetrics

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. 16w3d.

OB letter from 4/23 reviewed with her: HIV viral load 15,000, CD4 450, hep B and C negative, CBC at baseline. OB is working with ID on starting treatment. She has not heard from ID yet. Feels well, nausea better, no pain episodes, no fevers, no cough. Taking folic acid and the prenatal vitamin.

Vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, gravid, nontender. No edema.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. HIV in pregnancy, untreated. Re-sent the ID referral today marked urgent, copy to her OB clinic. Front desk will call ID Monday to confirm a date.
2. HbSS. CBC today. Reviewed warning signs: fever, chest pain, cough or shortness of breath, pain not settling at home. Go straight to the ED for any of those.
3. Pregnancy: OB following; next OB visit later this month.
I'll see her after the baby comes, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jada, your hemoglobin from Friday is steady, 9.4, about your usual. White count and platelets fine. Our front desk left ID a message this morning and will let you know the date.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Outside hospital discharge summary. Admitted 05/27/2026, discharged 05/31/2026. Received 06/03/2026.

Patient: 25-year-old G1 at about 19 weeks with HbSS sickle cell disease and HIV, not on antiretroviral therapy.
Allergy: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis risk).

Presented with fever and chest pain. Chest X-ray showed a new infiltrate, and oxygen saturation was low on room air. Admission hemoglobin 7.4.

Diagnosis: acute chest syndrome.

Course: ceftriaxone and azithromycin, supplemental oxygen, incentive spirometry and IV analgesia. Simple transfusion of 2 units packed red blood cells on hospital day 1 with steady improvement. Off oxygen before discharge. Fetal heart tones normal throughout; obstetrics followed daily. Discharge hemoglobin 9.2.

Discharge medications: folic acid 1 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
Follow-up: high-risk obstetrics within 1 week; primary care as scheduled. Continue incentive spirometry at home.

documents.title: home from hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted you to know I was in the hospital last week with acute chest. They gave me blood. Baby is ok. I'm home and seeing OB on Tuesday.

documents.title: RE: home from hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, Jada. Their summary came in yesterday. Glad you're home. Keep doing the breathing exercises and come in or go to the ED right away if the fever or chest pain comes back.

events.reason: Severe abdominal pain, 28 weeks pregnant, sickle cell disease

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside hospital ED physician record, seen 07/28/2026. Received 08/03/2026.

CC: abdominal pain.

HPI: 25-year-old G1 at 28 weeks 0 days with HbSS disease and HIV (not on antiretroviral therapy), about three months after her 04/23 prenatal visit. Six hours of severe abdominal pain, sharp and constant. Drank fluids and rested at home without relief. No vaginal bleeding or discharge. Two admissions this pregnancy for acute chest syndrome, each needing transfusion. Keeping up with her prenatal visits.

Meds: folic acid 1 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis risk).
Family history: brother with sickle cell disease; parents with sickle cell trait; paternal aunt with lupus.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Administrative assistant.

Triage: T 37.8 C (100.0 F), BP 130/85, HR 105, RR 22.

Exam: uncomfortable. Abdomen diffusely tender, no rebound, no guarding. Fetal heart tones normal.

Labs: hemoglobin 8.2 (her baseline 9.5), WBC 15.0, platelets 350. LDH 486. Total bilirubin 3.4, direct 0.4, indirect 3.0. Haptoglobin 8. Urinalysis unremarkable.

MDM: picture of an abdominal vaso-occlusive crisis with ongoing hemolysis in a 28-week pregnancy. IV fluids and IV opioid started. Obstetrics at bedside, fetal monitoring placed.

Impression: sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis.
Disposition: admitted to the antepartum unit.

events.reason: Vaso-occlusive crisis at 28 weeks; untreated HIV

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Outside hospital discharge summary. Admitted 07/28/2026, discharged 07/31/2026. Received 08/04/2026.

Admitting diagnosis: sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis, abdominal, at 28 weeks. Secondary: HIV in pregnancy, untreated; HbSS disease; two acute chest syndrome admissions earlier this pregnancy.
Allergy: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis risk).

Course: IV fluids and IV opioid analgesia with steady improvement; pain gone by day 3. Continuous fetal monitoring was reassuring. Hematology and maternal-fetal medicine followed. No transfusion this admission. Discharge hemoglobin 8.6.

Infectious Disease consulted on 07/29: HIV-1 viral load and resistance genotype sent. Treatment started the same day without waiting for the genotype, given the gestational age: dolutegravir 50 mg daily plus emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 200/25 mg daily. Counseled on daily adherence.

Discharge medications: dolutegravir 50 mg daily (new); emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 200/25 mg daily (new); folic acid 1 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily.
Follow-up: ID clinic in about 3 weeks; high-risk obstetrics within 1 week.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Clinic Letter
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease clinic. Visit 08/19/2026. Received 08/24/2026.

Dear colleague,

Ms. Owusu returned three weeks after we started her on dolutegravir 50 mg with emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 200/25 mg daily during her July admission. She is 31 weeks pregnant. She has missed no doses by her account and reports no side effects.

The resistance genotype sent in July showed no resistance mutations. Today's HIV-1 RNA is 290 copies/mL, down from 15,000 in April.

Plan: continue the same regimen. Repeat viral load in 4 weeks, and we will share results with obstetrics for delivery planning.

Allergies reviewed: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis risk).

Infectious Disease clinic
